title: Own Tile inserted into RPG Maker - Can't use it

posts.author: Venex
posts.body: I've created my own tile and copied it into the tilesets directory of my RPG Maker game. Now I have a  problem using it. I've created a new Tileset in the Database of my RPG Maker game, but I can't use it. The Pencil doesn't paint it.

posts.author: alasth
posts.body:

Hi
@Venex
We need more details to help you.
Have you ever imported someone else's tileset before and do you know how to create a new set in the database?
What resolution does your tileset have?
What format is it in?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
What type of tile is it (regular or autotile), and in which of the six different tilesheet formats did you place it where?
you can check the help files, but there are different formats for the tilesheets and each sheet will only work correctly in the correct slot

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
Yeah as Andar said, you can't just place a tile anyway.
Some tiles are auto tiles and work differently from single tiles.
If you want to use single tiles, then use A5 (normal) when importing it.
And when you say, tile, is it just one 48x48 image? You still have to follow the tile template even if it's just 1 tile.

posts.author: Venex
posts.body:
It now works when I use A5 (normal), because it is a single tile.
I imported it in A2 without following the tile template.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
inserting single tiles has other problems as well, the makers need full tilesheets to function properly.
and A5 is for regular tiles that are supposed to go to the ground layer on automated layering, MZ can simply switch to manual layering and have all regular tiles from B to E placed manually on the ground layer.
you'll do your maps a lot of favours if you learn how to exchange existing tiles that you don't need on existing tilesheets with your tiles.
and yes, A2 is for full non-animated autotiles (144x96 pixel), not for regular tiles (48x48 pixel).
